definitions: static fraction = 1 - (port cost with shrunk token-conditional mean-residual tables / destruction floor), per layer, on the 307k FineWeb audit at T=512

predictions.claim: The static fraction decays with depth overall, but NOT strictly monotonically: at least one deeper layer (boundary/positional-heavy) beats the layer above it.
predictions.note: Layer-1 archetypes were already boundary-dominated; some deep layers likely attend on document/sentence boundaries, which token tables capture well.

Block 1's output adds real context sensitivity (its pattern was worth +2.70), but the same argument at layer 1 did not stop tables from working; one more block of mixing should degrade tables only partially.

predictions.claim: By layer 9 the static fraction is below 0.80 — i.e. the ledger pipeline in its current static form does not extend to mid-depth.
Destruction floors are non-monotone in depth and at least one mid-or-late layer has a floor under 0.5 nats, i.e. much of the pattern stack is individually cheap.
predictions.note: Layer 1 at +2.70 looked exceptional in the doc (27x all of layer-0 attention); most layers are probably not like it.

decision_rule: The decay curve stands on its own as a result either way. If P3 fails high (static fraction stays above 0.8 deep), the ledger pipeline extends much further than assumed and experiments 2/9 rise in priority; if the curve collapses immediately at layer 2, the layer-1 landmark is a boundary effect of the first context-free read, and 'port the machinery deeper' dies early.
